\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter03.GoldreichLevinAlgorithm.Adaptive}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin Query State]
\lean{FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004
}
\label{FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord}
For a natural number $n$, a Goldreich–Levin query state consists of an optional finite
family of subsets of $[n]$ and a finite list of estimate records for $n$ coordinates.
The optional family is the active family, and each record contains a coordinate set, a
frequency prefix, and a rational estimate.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Failure in an estimate trace]
\lean{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.HasFailure}
\label{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.HasFailure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.IsAccurate, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let a trace be a finite list of estimate records of length
$n$, let the target be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, and let
$\tau$ be a rational threshold in $(0,1]$. The trace has a failure if it contains a
record that is not accurate for this target at threshold $\tau$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Failure in a query state]
\lean{FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.HasFailure}
\label{FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.HasFailure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.HasFailure, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let a query state consist of an optional active family of
subsets of the $n$ coordinates and a finite trace of estimate records, let the target be
a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, and let $\tau$ be a rational
threshold in $(0,1]$. The state has a failure if its trace contains a record for which
the absolute difference between its estimate and the restricted Fourier weight of the
target, at the record's coordinates and frequency prefix, is at least $\tau^2/4$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Query State Invariant]
\lean{FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.SatisfiesInvariant}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b002
}
\label{FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.SatisfiesInvariant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinActiveInvariant, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let a target Boolean function on $\\{−1,1\\}^n$ be given,
let $\\tau$ be rational with $0<\\tau\\leq1$, and let $k$ be a natural number. A query
state satisfies the invariant if there is a finite family $A$ of subsets of $[n]$ such
that its active family is exactly $A$, $A$ satisfies the Goldreich–Levin active
invariant for the target, $\\tau$, and $k$, and $|A|$ is at most the active-family cap
for $\\tau$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of the active cap]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap_pos}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap_pos}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap}
\difficulty{3}
For every rational number $\tau$ with $0<\tau\le 1$, the integer $\left\lceil
4/\tau^2\right\rceil$ is positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Initial query state invariant]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinInitialQueryState_satisfiesInvariant}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinInitialQueryState_satisfiesInvariant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.SatisfiesInvariant, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap_pos, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveInvariant_zero}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be any target function, and
let $0<\tau\le1$ be a rational threshold. The state whose active family is the singleton
containing the empty set and whose trace is empty satisfies the following at stage $0$:
its active family has size at most $\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$; every active set lies among
the first zero coordinates; every set $U$ with $\tau\le|\widehat f(U)|$ has its
restriction to the first zero coordinates in the active family; and every active set has
restricted Fourier weight greater than $\tau^2/4$ whenever the stage is positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Accuracy and absence of trace failures]
\lean{FABL.not_goldreichLevinEstimateTrace_hasFailure_iff}
\label{FABL.not_goldreichLevinEstimateTrace_hasFailure_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.HasFailure, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.IsAccurate, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let a trace be a finite list of estimate records on
the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, let the target be a sign-valued Boolean function on
that cube, and let the rational threshold $\tau$ satisfy $0<\tau\leq 1$. The trace has
no record whose estimate differs from the corresponding restricted Fourier weight by at
least $\tau^2/4$ if and only if every record in the trace has estimate error strictly
less than $\tau^2/4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin Query Step]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryStep}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryStep}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.goldreichLevinRefine, FABL.goldreichLevinTraceEstimate}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\\tau$ be rational with $0<\\tau\\leq1$, and let $k$
be a natural number with $k<n$. Given a query state and a finite list of estimate
records, append the records to the state's trace. The new active family is obtained by
applying the Goldreich–Levin refinement at level $k$ to the old active family, using the
estimate computed from the appended trace; if the old active family is absent, the new
active family is absent as well.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Failure characterization for one query step]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryStep_hasFailure_iff_of_not_hasFailure}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryStep_hasFailure_iff_of_not_hasFailure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.IsAccurate, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.HasFailure, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.HasFailure, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryStep}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, let $0<\tau\le1$, let $k<n$,
and let a query state have no inaccurate estimate in its trace. After appending a finite
list of estimate records and performing the query step at stage $k$, the resulting state
has an inaccurate estimate in its trace if and only if at least one record in the
appended list is inaccurate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Controller step work bound]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinControllerStepWork}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinControllerStepWork}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap}
For a natural number $n$ and a rational threshold $\tau$ in $(0,1]$, define the
controller step work to be $16(n+1)^2(A(\tau)+1)^2$, where $A(\tau)$ is the active cap at
threshold $\tau$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin stage step program]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinStageStepProgram}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p089-b009,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p090-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p090-b005
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinStageStepProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.LearningProgram.map, FABL.goldreichLevinControllerStepWork, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryStep, FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram}
For a dimension $n$, a threshold $\tau\in(0,1]$, an index $k<n$, a query state, and a
finite family of active frequency sets, the stage step program uses the Goldreich–Levin
stage estimates for that family to update the state at stage $k$, while charging the
controller’s prescribed step work.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Cost law for a Goldreich–Levin stage]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_goldreichLevinStageStepProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_goldreichLevinStageStepProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost_map, FABL.goldreichLevinControllerStepWork, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryStep, FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinStageStepProgram}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a target function, let
$\tau\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $0<\tau\le1$, let $k<n$, and let the current state consist of
an optional finite active family of coordinate subsets and a finite trace of estimate
records. For any finite active family supplied to the stage, the law of the stage-step
program is the image of the stage-estimate program's outcome law under the map that
appends its estimate records to the state trace, updates the active family according to
the Goldreich–Levin refinement rule, and adds controller work $16(n+1)^2(C+1)^2$ to the
work cost, where $C=\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stage failure probability identity]
\lean{FABL.outerEventProbability_goldreichLevinStageStepProgram_failure}
\label{FABL.outerEventProbability_goldreichLevinStageStepProgram_failure}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.IsAccurate, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.HasFailure, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram.outerEventProbability, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryStep_hasFailure_iff_of_not_hasFailure, FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram, FABL.goldreichLevinStageStepProgram, FABL.runWithCost_goldreichLevinStageStepProgram}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $0<\tau<1$ be a
Goldreich–Levin threshold, and let $k<n$. Given a query state $s$ with no inaccurate
estimate record and a finite active family of frequencies, the probability that one
stage step produces a state containing an inaccurate record equals the probability that
the stage estimation program produces a list containing an inaccurate record. Accuracy
is measured against the restricted Fourier weight, with tolerance $\tau^2/4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Stage failure budget]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinStageFailureBudget}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinStageFailureBudget}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence}
For a natural number $n$ and a rational threshold $\tau$ in $(0,1]$, define the stage
failure budget as $2A(\tau)$ times the nonnegative extended real number obtained by
taking the nonnegative part of the real value of the first component of the
call-confidence interval at $(n,\tau)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Goldreich–Levin failure budget]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinFailureBudget_rat_le_one_twentieth}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinFailureBudget_rat_le_one_twentieth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$ and rational threshold $\tau$ with $0<\tau\le 1$, let
$A=\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$ and $\delta=1/[40(n+1)(A+1)]$. Then $n\cdot(2A)\cdot\delta\le
1/20$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Goldreich–Levin query run through a stage]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p083-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p085-b004
}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.LearningProgram.bind, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinStageStepProgram}
For a dimension $n$ and threshold $\tau\in(0,1]$, the query program run through stage
$k$ is defined for each $k\le n$. At stage zero it returns the state with active family
$\{\varnothing\}$ and empty trace; at each subsequent stage it leaves a state with no
active family unchanged, performs the stage step when the active family has size at most
the active cap, and otherwise returns a state with no active family and the same trace.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Goldreich–Levin failure probability bound]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo_outerFailureProbability_le}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo_outerFailureProbability_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord.IsAccurate, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateTrace.HasFailure, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState.HasFailure, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningProgram.outerEventProbability, FABL.LearningProgram.outerEventProbability_bind_le_add, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.card_goldreichLevinCandidates_le_two_mul, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo, FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram_outerFailureProbability_le, FABL.goldreichLevinStageFailureBudget, FABL.goldreichLevinStageStepProgram, FABL.outerEventProbability_goldreichLevinStageStepProgram_failure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and
let $0<\tau\le 1$. For every natural number $k\le n$, the outer probability that the run
of the Goldreich–Levin query algorithm through stage $k$ has an inaccurate estimate is
at most $k$ times the stage failure budget.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Projected cost bound for partial runs]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo_costProjection_le}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo_costProjection_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinEstimateRecord, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.addOutcomeCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost_bind, FABL.card_goldreichLevinCandidates_le_two_mul, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinCandidates, FABL.goldreichLevinControllerStepWork, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo, FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram, FABL.runWithCost_goldreichLevinStageStepProgram}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function,
and let $0<\tau\le1$ be a rational threshold. Suppose $P$ maps learning costs to natural
numbers, satisfies $P(0)=0$ and $P(c+d)=P(c)+P(d)$ for all costs $c,d$, and let $B$ be a
natural number such that, for every $k<n$, every active family of subsets of
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and every supported outcome of the corresponding stage-estimation
program, the projected cost is at most $B$ times the number of candidates in that stage.
Then for every $k\le n$, every supported outcome of the algorithm run through $k$ stages
has projected cost at most
$k\bigl(P(16(n+1)^2(\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil+1)^2)+2\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil B\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Goldreich–Levin query complexity bound]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo_queries_le}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo_queries_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo_costProjection_le, FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram_queries_le, FABL.goldreichLevinWeightAccuracy}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, let
$0<\tau\le 1$, and let $k\le n$. Every outcome in the support of the run through stage
$k$, including its recorded learning costs, uses at most $k\cdot
2\,\mathrm{cap}(\tau)\cdot 2m$ membership queries, where
$\mathrm{cap}(\tau)=\left\lceil4/\tau^2\right\rceil$ and $m$ is the estimator sample
count at accuracy $\tau^2/4$ and confidence parameter
$\gamma=1/[40(n+1)(\mathrm{cap}(\tau)+1)]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Goldreich–Levin work bound]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo_work_le}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo_work_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.GoldreichLevinQueryState, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.goldreichLevinActiveCap, FABL.goldreichLevinCallConfidence, FABL.goldreichLevinControllerStepWork, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo, FABL.goldreichLevinQueryRunUpTo_costProjection_le, FABL.goldreichLevinStageEstimateProgram_work_le, FABL.goldreichLevinWeightAccuracy}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, let
$0<\tau\le1$, and let $k\le n$. Every outcome in the support of the run through stage
$k$, including its recorded learning costs, has local work at most
$k\bigl(W+2\,\mathrm{cap}(\tau)\cdot 8(m+1)(n+1)\bigr)$, where
$\mathrm{cap}(\tau)=\left\lceil4/\tau^2\right\rceil$,
$W=16(n+1)^2(\mathrm{cap}(\tau)+1)^2$, and $m$ is the estimator sample count at accuracy
$\tau^2/4$ and confidence parameter $1/[40(n+1)(\mathrm{cap}(\tau)+1)]$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, and
let $0<\tau\le 1$. For every $k\le n$ and every state-and-cost outcome in the support of
the randomized query procedure run through stage $k$, if the state’s trace contains no
estimate whose error in restricted Fourier weight is at least $\tau^2/4$, then there is
an active family $\mathcal A$ of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ such that the state
records $\mathcal A$ as its active family, every member of $\mathcal A$ is contained in
$\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, and every Fourier coefficient of $f$ with magnitude at least $\tau$
has its intersection with $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$ in $\mathcal A$. Moreover, when $k>0$,
every $S\in\mathcal A$ has restricted Fourier weight greater than $\tau^2/4$ for the
first $k$ coordinates and frequency $S\cap\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, and $|\mathcal
A|\le\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Completeness of the active family]
\lean{FABL.goldreichLevinActiveInvariant_complete}
\label{FABL.goldreichLevinActiveInvariant_complete}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.GoldreichLevinActiveInvariant, FABL.GoldreichLevinThreshold, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.prefixFrequency_eq_self}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $\tau$ be rational
with $0<\tau\le 1$. Suppose a finite family $\mathcal A$ of subsets of the $n$
coordinates has the property that every frequency set $U$ whose Fourier coefficient for
$f$ has magnitude at least $\tau$ has its length-$n$ prefix in $\mathcal A$. Then every
such $U$ belongs to $\mathcal A$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let $\tau$ be rational
with $0<\tau\le 1$. Suppose a finite family $\mathcal A$ of subsets of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ satisfies all three conditions: every member is contained in the full
coordinate set; every frequency set $U$ whose Fourier coefficient for $f$ has magnitude
at least $\tau$ belongs to $\mathcal A$; and, for every $S\in\mathcal A$, the restricted
Fourier weight associated with the full coordinate set and the part of $S$ in that set
is strictly greater than $\tau^2/4$. Then $|\mathcal A|\le 4/\tau^2$.
\end{theorem}
